POSP System Workflows, Regulatory Rules &
Policy Reference Manual
Comprehensive knowledge base for resolving Point of Sales Person (POSP) onboarding, portal
navigation, compliance, and policy issuance queries.
Domain: Insurance Distribution
(POSP)
Regulatory Authority: IRDAI
Guidelines
Document Scope: System & Policy
Operations
Note on Source Scope: No external attachment files were transmitted in the prompt payload. This
knowledge base synthesizes standard Indian insurance POSP operational workflows, IRDAI Point of
Sales regulatory guidelines, system troubleshooting protocols, and policy servicing rules. Platform-specific
credentials, commission slabs, and internal ticket routing URLs are marked with bracketed placeholders
for organization-specific customization.
1. Regulatory Framework & POSP Eligibility Rules
A Point of Sales Person (POSP) is an individual authorized by an insurer or insurance intermediary
(such as an Insurance Broker or Corporate Agent) under the Insurance Regulatory and Development
Authority of India (IRDAI) guidelines to solicit and market pre-underwritten, simple insurance
products.
1.1 Mandatory Eligibility Criteria
Minimum Age: The applicant must have completed at least 18 years of age on the date of
application submission.
Educational Qualification: The applicant must have passed at least Class 10 (Secondary School
Examination) or an equivalent examination from a recognized educational board.
Exclusivity Rule (Single-Entity Mapping): Under IRDAI regulations, an individual can act as a
POSP for only one insurer or one insurance intermediary at any given time. Dual registration
across multiple brokers or insurers is strictly prohibited and automatically blocked via PAN-level
validation on the IRDAI IIB (Insurance Information Bureau) portal.
Conflict of Interest Restriction: Existing licensed insurance agents, employees of insurance
companies, or directors/partners of licensed intermediaries cannot register as POSPs unless they
formally surrender their existing license and obtain a No Objection Certificate (NOC).
1.2 Permitted Insurance Products (POSP Scope)
POSPs are strictly restricted to soliciting pre-underwritten products approved by IRDAI under the
POS category. Complex commercial lines or products requiring manual medical/financial underwriting
fall outside POSP authority.

2. End-to-End POSP Onboarding & Certification Workflow
The digital onboarding lifecycle transitions an applicant from registration to an active, certified POSP
code capable of issuing policies and earning commissions.
2.1 Step-by-Step System Onboarding Stages
1. Stage 1 — Lead Registration & Mobile/Email Verification: Applicant registers on [POSP
Portal URL] using their legal name (matching PAN), mobile number, and email address. OTP
authentication verifies contact ownership.
2. Stage 2 — KYC & Document Upload: Applicant submits mandatory KYC documents and bank
details for payout mapping. Automated OCR extracts data fields and cross-validates against NSDL
(PAN) and bank penny-drop APIs.
3. Stage 3 — IIB Blacklist & Deduplication Check: The system queries the Insurance Information
Bureau (IIB) database using the applicant's PAN and Aadhaar hash to confirm the applicant is not
active with another intermediary or blacklisted for fraud.
POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual Page 2 of 7
4. Stage 4 — Mandatory 15-Hour Training: Once KYC is approved, the Learning Management
System (LMS) unlocks the mandatory 15-hour IRDAI-prescribed training modules (covering
General Insurance, Life Insurance, or both). The system enforces strict timer tracking; fast-
forwarding videos or skipping slides is disabled.
5. Stage 5 — Online Certification Examination: Upon completing 15 hours of logged study time,
the applicant unlocks the online assessment. The exam consists of 50 multiple-choice questions
(1 mark each) with a 60-minute duration. A minimum score of 35% (18 out of 50 marks) is
required to pass.
6. Stage 6 — Agreement E-Sign & POSP Code Generation: Passing candidates execute the
POSP Agency/Brokerage Agreement via Aadhaar e-Sign. The system generates a unique POSP
Code (e.g., [POSP-ID-FORMAT] ) and issues the downloadable POSP Certificate.

3. System Operations, Portal Modules & Troubleshooting
This section defines system behaviors, error codes, and operational resolutions for support teams
and RAG automated responses.
POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual Page 3 of 7
3.1 Core Portal Modules
Dashboard & Business Summary: Displays active POSP status, total policies issued, gross
written premium (GWP), pending renewals, and earned payout summary for the current financial
month.
Quote & Proposal Engine: Multi-insurer comparison engine for Motor, Health, and Term plans.
Fetches vehicle registration details via VAHAN integration using registration number, engine
number, and chassis number.
Endorsement & Servicing Desk: Allows POSPs to raise post-issuance modification requests
(name correction, nominee update, address change, NCB rectification, or policy cancellation).
Payout & Ledger Module: Tracks commission statements, TDS deductions (under Section
194D/194H as applicable), GST invoices (if GST-registered), and UTR bank settlement
references.

4. Policy Issuance, Underwriting & Servicing Rules
POSPs must adhere strictly to underwriting rules during policy solicitation to prevent claim
repudiation or policy voidance.
4.1 Motor Insurance Rules (Break-in, NCB & Transfer)
Break-in Policy Inspection: If a Comprehensive/Own Damage (OD) motor policy has expired
(even by 1 day), the vehicle enters "Break-in" status. Physical or self-video pre-inspection is
mandatory before OD coverage can be bound. Third-Party (TP) liability coverage can be issued
immediately without inspection, subject to a T+1 or T+2 risk inception waiting rule applied by
specific insurers.
No Claim Bonus (NCB) Rules: NCB belongs to the insured person, not the vehicle. NCB slabs
progress as 0% (Year 1), 20% (Year 2), 25% (Year 3), 35% (Year 4), 45% (Year 5), and 50% (Year
6+). NCB lapses completely if a policy is not renewed within 90 days of expiry or if an Own
Damage claim is lodged during the policy period.
Wrong NCB Declaration: If a customer claims an NCB discount inaccurately, the insurer will
issue an NCB Recovery Notice. Until the differential premium plus applicable penalty is paid, Own
Damage claims remain strictly inadmissible.
Ownership Transfer: Upon sale of a vehicle, the buyer must apply for transfer of the insurance
policy within 14 days of RTO RC transfer by submitting the transferred RC, Form 29/30, and
differential NCB payment (since the seller's NCB does not transfer to the buyer).
4.2 Health & Life Insurance Rules
Pre-Existing Diseases (PED): Any condition, ailment, or injury diagnosed or treated within 36
months (or 48 months depending on policy wording) prior to policy inception must be declared
truthfully in the proposal form. Non-disclosure of material health facts constitutes fraud and leads
to policy cancellation without refund.
Free-Look Period: Customers have a statutory 30-day free-look period (for policies solicited via
distance/electronic mode, or 15–30 days per current IRDAI Master Circular on Health/Life) from
the date of receipt of the policy document to review terms and cancel for a pro-rata refund (less
medical/stamp duty charges) if dissatisfied.
Grace Period for Renewals: Health insurance policies carry a 30-day grace period from the due
date to renew without losing continuity benefits (waiting period credits). However, coverage does
not apply during the unpaid grace period days.
POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual Page 5 of 7
4.3 Endorsements & Policy Cancellation
Non-Financial Endorsements: Minor spelling corrections in name, address updates,
phone/email updates, nominee changes, and correction of engine/chassis typos (with RC proof)
require no additional premium.
Financial Endorsements: Addition of CNG/LPG kit, increase in IDV, addition of zero-
depreciation/consumables add-ons, or NCB correction require differential premium payment
before the endorsement schedule is issued.
Cancellation Rules: Motor TP policies cannot be cancelled unless the vehicle is certified
scrapped/total loss or covered under double insurance (another valid policy covering the exact
same period). Motor OD policies can be cancelled on a short-period scale if no claim has been
made.
5. Code of Conduct, Compliance & Commission Governance
Every POSP is bound by the IRDAI Code of Conduct. Violations result in immediate POSP code
suspension, forfeiture of accrued commissions, and permanent blacklisting on the IIB portal.
5.1 Strict Prohibitions (Zero-Tolerance Violations)
Rebating (Section 41 of Insurance Act, 1938): Offering any cash-back, gift, discount, or
commission sharing to a customer to induce them to buy a policy is a punishable statutory
offense.
Premium Collection in Personal Account: POSPs are strictly forbidden from collecting
insurance premiums in their personal bank accounts, UPI IDs, or cash (beyond statutory limits)
and paying via their own cards. All premiums must flow directly from the customer's bank/payment
instrument to the insurer's payment gateway.
Mis-selling & False Promises: Misrepresenting policy terms, hiding waiting periods, or
guaranteeing non-guaranteed returns is prohibited.
Unauthorized Document Tampering: Altering previous year policy PDFs, forging RC books, or
uploading manipulated inspection videos results in immediate termination and legal action.
5.2 Commission & Payout Rules
Payout Eligibility: Commissions are calculated on Net Premium (excluding GST) for verified,
active policies that have cleared the free-look/cancellation window.
Clawback Policy: If a policy is cancelled, dishonored (cheque bounce), or voided due to
fraud/non-disclosure, 100% of the commission paid on that policy is clawed back and adjusted
against future payouts.
Taxation (TDS & GST): Income tax (TDS) is deducted at applicable statutory rates (e.g., 2% or
5% under Income Tax Act provisions, or 20% if PAN is invalid/inoperative). POSPs whose
aggregate turnover crosses the statutory GST threshold must furnish a valid GSTIN and raise
compliant tax invoices to claim GST reimbursement.
POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual Page 6 of 7
6. Golden Q&A Reference Set for RAG Grounding
The following standardized question-answer pairs establish canonical responses for high-frequency
user queries.
Q1: I completed my 15-hour training, why is the exam button still locked?
Answer: The exam button unlocks only when two conditions are met: (1) all training modules show
100% completion status, and (2) the cumulative active session timer equals at least 15 hours (900
minutes). If individual slides were read faster than 15 hours total, re-open any module and review
the summary material until the timer reaches 15:00:00, then refresh the dashboard.
Q2: Can I work as a POSP if I already hold a regular LIC or General Insurance individual
agent license?
Answer: No. Under IRDAI regulations, an individual cannot simultaneously hold an Individual
Insurance Agent license and a POSP registration. You must formally surrender your existing
agency license, obtain a Clearance/Release Certificate, and ensure your PAN is delisted from the
IRDAI IIB portal before your POSP code can be activated.
Q3: A customer sold their car and wants to transfer their 50% NCB to their newly purchased
car. How does the system handle this?
Answer: NCB stays with the seller, not the sold car. The seller must first obtain an NCB Reserving
Letter from the previous insurer (valid for 3 years) by submitting proof of vehicle sale (transferred
RC or Form 29/30 and policy cancellation/endorsement proof). During new car quote generation,
select the earned NCB slab (50%) and upload the NCB Reserving Letter for underwriting approval.
Q4: Why was my policy payout held or reversed in the ledger?
Answer: Payouts are held or reversed if: (1) the customer cancelled the policy within the free-look
period, (2) a motor policy was cancelled due to duplicate insurance or wrong NCB declaration, (3)
KYC/bank account status changed to invalid, or (4) the insurer flagged a compliance discrepancy.
Check the "Ledger Remarks" column in the Payout module for the exact policy-level reason code.
Q5: Can I issue a health insurance policy with a ₹15 Lakh Sum Insured using my POSP
code?
Answer: No. Under IRDAI POSP guidelines, pre-underwritten POS health insurance products are
capped at the prescribed Sum Insured limit (standard ₹5 Lakhs limit unless specifically enhanced
by an IRDAI product circular for a designated plan). Policies exceeding POS thresholds must be
sourced through non-POS/regular licensed channels.
POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual Page 7 of 7

Common Rejection Triggers: Admit card/hall ticket uploaded instead of mark sheet, provisional certificate without roll number, or cropped board seal.

Document Type: Bank Proof
Acceptance Criteria: Personalized cancelled cheque (with printed account holder name), bank passbook front page, or stamped bank statement.
Common Rejection Triggers: Non-personalized cheque without printed name, invalid IFSC code, joint account where applicant is secondary holder, or NRE account.

Document Type: Photograph
Acceptance Criteria: Recent passport-size color photograph against a plain light background with face clearly visible.
Common Rejection Triggers: Selfies, sunglasses/caps, group photos, or dark/low-resolution images.

chunks.subsection: 3.1 Core Portal Modules
chunks.text:
3.1 Core Portal Modules
Dashboard & Business Summary: Displays active POSP status, total policies issued, gross
written premium (GWP), pending renewals, and earned payout summary for the current financial
month.
Quote & Proposal Engine: Multi-insurer comparison engine for Motor, Health, and Term plans.
Fetches vehicle registration details via VAHAN integration using registration number, engine
number, and chassis number.
Endorsement & Servicing Desk: Allows POSPs to raise post-issuance modification requests
(name correction, nominee update, address change, NCB rectification, or policy cancellation).
Payout & Ledger Module: Tracks commission statements, TDS deductions (under Section
194D/194H as applicable), GST invoices (if GST-registered), and UTR bank settlement
references.

chunks.subsection: 3.2 System Error Matrix & Resolution Protocols / PAN Already Exists / IIB Active Flag
chunks.text:
System Symptom / Error: PAN Already Exists / IIB Active Flag
Root Cause: Applicant's PAN is currently mapped to another insurer, corporate agent, or broker on the IRDAI IIB portal.
Standard Resolution Steps: Applicant must request formal termination and an NOC/Release Letter from the previous organization. Upload the NOC to [Compliance Ticket Queue] to re- trigger IIB verification once the previous entity delists the PAN.

chunks.document_name: POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual
chunks.subsection: 3.2 System Error Matrix & Resolution Protocols / Training Timer Not Progressing
chunks.text:
System Symptom / Error: Training Timer Not Progressing
Root Cause: Browser tab switched/minimized, idle timeout triggered, or unstable internet disconnecting heartbeat pings.
Standard Resolution Steps: Keep the LMS browser tab active in the foreground; disable ad-blockers/script blockers; refresh the module every 30 minutes to ensure session synchronization.

chunks.document_name: POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual
chunks.subsection: 3.2 System Error Matrix & Resolution Protocols / Bank Penny-Drop Failure
chunks.text:
System Symptom / Error: Bank Penny-Drop Failure
Root Cause: Name mismatch between PAN and Bank CBS record, dormant account, or incorrect IFSC code after bank merger.
Standard Resolution Steps: Verify updated IFSC code; ensure bank account is an active resident savings/current account in the applicant's sole/primary name; re-upload a clear cancelled cheque.

chunks.document_name: POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual
chunks.subsection: 3.2 System Error Matrix & Resolution Protocols / VAHAN Fetch Timeout / Vehicle Not Found
chunks.text:
System Symptom / Error: VAHAN Fetch Timeout / Vehicle Not Found
Root Cause: RTO database API latency, newly registered vehicle not yet synced, or commercial vehicle sub-class mismatch.
Standard Resolution Steps: Select "Manual Vehicle Entry" option, enter Make, Model, Variant, Fuel Type, Cubic Capacity, and Registration Date manually from the Registration Certificate (RC), and upload RC copy.

chunks.text:
System Symptom / Error: Payment Deducted, Policy Not Generated
Root Cause: Payment gateway webhook delay or insurer core system timeout during policy PDF generation.
Standard Resolution Steps: Wait 30 minutes for automated reconciliation cron job. Do not make a duplicate payment. Check "Pending Issuance" tab; if unresolved after 2 hours, raise a ticket with Payment Transaction ID.

chunks.document_name: POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual
chunks.text:
4. Policy Issuance, Underwriting & Servicing Rules
POSPs must adhere strictly to underwriting rules during policy solicitation to prevent claim
repudiation or policy voidance.

chunks.document_name: POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual
chunks.subsection: 4.1 Motor Insurance Rules (Break-in, NCB & Transfer)
chunks.text:
4.1 Motor Insurance Rules (Break-in, NCB & Transfer)
Break-in Policy Inspection: If a Comprehensive/Own Damage (OD) motor policy has expired
(even by 1 day), the vehicle enters "Break-in" status. Physical or self-video pre-inspection is
mandatory before OD coverage can be bound. Third-Party (TP) liability coverage can be issued
immediately without inspection, subject to a T+1 or T+2 risk inception waiting rule applied by
specific insurers.
No Claim Bonus (NCB) Rules: NCB belongs to the insured person, not the vehicle. NCB slabs
progress as 0% (Year 1), 20% (Year 2), 25% (Year 3), 35% (Year 4), 45% (Year 5), and 50% (Year
6+). NCB lapses completely if a policy is not renewed within 90 days of expiry or if an Own
Damage claim is lodged during the policy period.
Wrong NCB Declaration: If a customer claims an NCB discount inaccurately, the insurer will
issue an NCB Recovery Notice. Until the differential premium plus applicable penalty is paid, Own
Damage claims remain strictly inadmissible.
Ownership Transfer: Upon sale of a vehicle, the buyer must apply for transfer of the insurance
policy within 14 days of RTO RC transfer by submitting the transferred RC, Form 29/30, and
differential NCB payment (since the seller's NCB does not transfer to the buyer).

chunks.document_name: POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual
chunks.subsection: 4.2 Health & Life Insurance Rules
chunks.text:
4.2 Health & Life Insurance Rules
Pre-Existing Diseases (PED): Any condition, ailment, or injury diagnosed or treated within 36
months (or 48 months depending on policy wording) prior to policy inception must be declared
truthfully in the proposal form. Non-disclosure of material health facts constitutes fraud and leads
to policy cancellation without refund.
Free-Look Period: Customers have a statutory 30-day free-look period (for policies solicited via
distance/electronic mode, or 15–30 days per current IRDAI Master Circular on Health/Life) from
the date of receipt of the policy document to review terms and cancel for a pro-rata refund (less
medical/stamp duty charges) if dissatisfied.
Grace Period for Renewals: Health insurance policies carry a 30-day grace period from the due
date to renew without losing continuity benefits (waiting period credits). However, coverage does
not apply during the unpaid grace period days.

chunks.document_name: POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual
chunks.subsection: 3.2 System Error Matrix & Resolution Protocols / CKYC Verification Failed During Proposal
chunks.text:
System Symptom / Error: CKYC Verification Failed During Proposal
Root Cause: Customer's PAN/Aadhaar details do not match Central KYC Registry records or customer lacks an existing CKYC number.
Standard Resolution Steps: Switch to "OVD (Officially Valid Document) Upload" flow, capture customer's live selfie/photo, PAN, and Aadhaar, and submit for insurer KYC approval.

chunks.document_name: POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual
chunks.subsection: 4.3 Endorsements & Policy Cancellation
chunks.text:
4.3 Endorsements & Policy Cancellation
Non-Financial Endorsements: Minor spelling corrections in name, address updates,
phone/email updates, nominee changes, and correction of engine/chassis typos (with RC proof)
require no additional premium.
Financial Endorsements: Addition of CNG/LPG kit, increase in IDV, addition of zero-
depreciation/consumables add-ons, or NCB correction require differential premium payment
before the endorsement schedule is issued.
Cancellation Rules: Motor TP policies cannot be cancelled unless the vehicle is certified
scrapped/total loss or covered under double insurance (another valid policy covering the exact
same period). Motor OD policies can be cancelled on a short-period scale if no claim has been
made.

chunks.document_name: POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual
chunks.section: 5. Code of Conduct, Compliance & Commission Governance
chunks.text:
5. Code of Conduct, Compliance & Commission Governance
Every POSP is bound by the IRDAI Code of Conduct. Violations result in immediate POSP code
suspension, forfeiture of accrued commissions, and permanent blacklisting on the IIB portal.

chunks.document_name: POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual
chunks.section: 5. Code of Conduct, Compliance & Commission Governance
chunks.subsection: 5.1 Strict Prohibitions (Zero-Tolerance Violations)
chunks.text:
5.1 Strict Prohibitions (Zero-Tolerance Violations)
Rebating (Section 41 of Insurance Act, 1938): Offering any cash-back, gift, discount, or
commission sharing to a customer to induce them to buy a policy is a punishable statutory
offense.
Premium Collection in Personal Account: POSPs are strictly forbidden from collecting
insurance premiums in their personal bank accounts, UPI IDs, or cash (beyond statutory limits)
and paying via their own cards. All premiums must flow directly from the customer's bank/payment
instrument to the insurer's payment gateway.
Mis-selling & False Promises: Misrepresenting policy terms, hiding waiting periods, or
guaranteeing non-guaranteed returns is prohibited.
Unauthorized Document Tampering: Altering previous year policy PDFs, forging RC books, or
uploading manipulated inspection videos results in immediate termination and legal action.

chunks.document_name: POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual
chunks.section: 5. Code of Conduct, Compliance & Commission Governance
chunks.subsection: 5.2 Commission & Payout Rules
chunks.text:
5.2 Commission & Payout Rules
Payout Eligibility: Commissions are calculated on Net Premium (excluding GST) for verified,
active policies that have cleared the free-look/cancellation window.
Clawback Policy: If a policy is cancelled, dishonored (cheque bounce), or voided due to
fraud/non-disclosure, 100% of the commission paid on that policy is clawed back and adjusted
against future payouts.
Taxation (TDS & GST): Income tax (TDS) is deducted at applicable statutory rates (e.g., 2% or
5% under Income Tax Act provisions, or 20% if PAN is invalid/inoperative). POSPs whose
aggregate turnover crosses the statutory GST threshold must furnish a valid GSTIN and raise
compliant tax invoices to claim GST reimbursement.

chunks.document_name: POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual
chunks.section: 6. Golden Q&A Reference Set for RAG Grounding
chunks.text:
6. Golden Q&A Reference Set for RAG Grounding
The following standardized question-answer pairs establish canonical responses for high-frequency
user queries.

chunks.document_name: POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual
chunks.section: 6. Golden Q&A Reference Set for RAG Grounding
chunks.text:
Q1: I completed my 15-hour training, why is the exam button still locked?
Answer: The exam button unlocks only when two conditions are met: (1) all training modules show
100% completion status, and (2) the cumulative active session timer equals at least 15 hours (900
minutes). If individual slides were read faster than 15 hours total, re-open any module and review
the summary material until the timer reaches 15:00:00, then refresh the dashboard.

chunks.document_name: POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual
chunks.section: 6. Golden Q&A Reference Set for RAG Grounding
chunks.text:
Q2: Can I work as a POSP if I already hold a regular LIC or General Insurance individual
agent license?
Answer: No. Under IRDAI regulations, an individual cannot simultaneously hold an Individual
Insurance Agent license and a POSP registration. You must formally surrender your existing
agency license, obtain a Clearance/Release Certificate, and ensure your PAN is delisted from the
IRDAI IIB portal before your POSP code can be activated.

chunks.document_name: POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual
chunks.section: 6. Golden Q&A Reference Set for RAG Grounding
chunks.text:
Q3: A customer sold their car and wants to transfer their 50% NCB to their newly purchased
car. How does the system handle this?
Answer: NCB stays with the seller, not the sold car. The seller must first obtain an NCB Reserving
Letter from the previous insurer (valid for 3 years) by submitting proof of vehicle sale (transferred
RC or Form 29/30 and policy cancellation/endorsement proof). During new car quote generation,
select the earned NCB slab (50%) and upload the NCB Reserving Letter for underwriting approval.

chunks.document_name: POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual
chunks.section: 6. Golden Q&A Reference Set for RAG Grounding
chunks.text:
Q4: Why was my policy payout held or reversed in the ledger?
Answer: Payouts are held or reversed if: (1) the customer cancelled the policy within the free-look
period, (2) a motor policy was cancelled due to duplicate insurance or wrong NCB declaration, (3)
KYC/bank account status changed to invalid, or (4) the insurer flagged a compliance discrepancy.
Check the "Ledger Remarks" column in the Payout module for the exact policy-level reason code.

chunks.document_name: POSP RAG System Knowledge Base & Policy Manual
chunks.section: 6. Golden Q&A Reference Set for RAG Grounding
chunks.text:
Q5: Can I issue a health insurance policy with a ₹15 Lakh Sum Insured using my POSP
code?
Answer: No. Under IRDAI POSP guidelines, pre-underwritten POS health insurance products are
capped at the prescribed Sum Insured limit (standard ₹5 Lakhs limit unless specifically enhanced
by an IRDAI product circular for a designated plan). Policies exceeding POS thresholds must be
sourced through non-POS/regular licensed channels.
